hero.description: Blue Lagoon 1 and Tham Phu Kham work because they are two different experiences in one stop: water and shade below, then a steep limestone climb to a large cave with a reclining Buddha inside.
steps: Swim first or save it for after the cave
Carry a proper torch for the cave
hero.rhythmNote: Do not treat the lagoon as the whole attraction. The cave climb is what turns this into a stronger half-day stop, but only if you have suitable shoes and enough light.

chapters.label: THE TWO PARTS
chapters.title: The lagoon is the reset; the cave is the exploration
chapters.body: The official tourism description places Tham Phu Kham about six kilometres from Vang Vieng and describes a steep climb of roughly 200 metres to the cave entrance. Below, the lagoon gives the visit an easy social side; above, the cave changes the pace completely.

chapters.label: THE CAVE
chapters.title: Bring light before you need it
chapters.body: Inside Tham Phu Kham there is no reason to push deeper than your light, footwear and confidence allow. The main cavern is known for its reclining Buddha, while darker sections quickly become a genuine cave environment rather than a lit tourist corridor.

note.label: ATLAS NOTE
note.text: Blue Lagoon 1 is famous; Tham Phu Kham is what makes the stop more than a swim.

chapters.label: CROWD RHYTHM
chapters.title: Morning changes the experience more than another activity does
chapters.body: Blue Lagoon 1 is one of Vang Vieng's best-known stops and can feel busy. An earlier arrival gives you a calmer lagoon and cooler conditions for the climb before you decide how long to stay in the water.

beforeYouLeave.title: Do not arrive with only swimwear
beforeYouLeave.body: The cave approach is steep enough that footwear matters. Pack for the cave first and the lagoon second: shoes with grip, water and a torch make the whole stop more useful.

items.label: From Vang Vieng
items.detail: The official tourism page places the cave across the river in the west-bank countryside.

items.label: Cave approach
items.detail: The official description notes roughly a 200 m climb to the entrance; take it slowly in heat or rain.

items.label: Inside
items.detail: The cave is not a simple fully lit walkway. Carry a dedicated light and stay within your comfort level.

items.label: Time
items.detail: This gives enough room for the lagoon, cave climb and a relaxed return.

faq.question: Is Blue Lagoon 1 the same stop as Tham Phu Kham Cave?
faq.answer: They are part of the same outing area. The lagoon sits below while the cave is reached by a steep climb above it.

faq.question: Do I need a torch for Tham Phu Kham?
faq.answer: Yes. Bring a proper torch if you intend to go beyond the brighter entrance area.

faq.question: How much time should I allow?
faq.answer: Treat the combination as a half-day stop if you want both the cave and the lagoon without rushing.

faq.question: Is the cave climb easy?
faq.answer: No. It is short compared with a long trek but steep and uneven, so shoes with grip are strongly preferable.

faq.question: When is the best time to go?
faq.answer: Morning is the cleanest rhythm: cooler climbing conditions and usually more space before the lagoon gets busier.
